verdict: Labcorp grew revenue 7% to $3.8B as both its diagnostics and biopharma lab businesses expanded, and it raised full-year guidance — though GAAP profit was nearly flat as amortization and restructuring costs weighed.

segments.name: Diagnostics Laboratories
segments.note: Everyday and specialty lab testing for doctors, hospitals and patients — up 6.5%, with 4.4% organic growth and 2.2 points from acquisitions.

segments.name: Biopharma Laboratory Services
segments.note: Central-lab testing that supports drug trials for pharmaceutical companies. Reported segment revenue was $867M, up 8.5%; shown here net of $6M of intercompany eliminations so the segments sum to consolidated revenue.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Sales, billing and the back office — Labcorp's SG&A line.

opex.name: Amortization of intangibles
opex.note: Spreading the cost of past acquisitions (customer relationships and other intangibles) over their useful lives.

opex.name: Restructuring & other charges
opex.note: Costs from reshaping the business, including its efficiency program.

otherDetail: Net other expense of $74M: interest expense of $59M, an $11M equity-method loss and $5M of other expense, partly offset by $1M of investment income.

takeaways.title: Growth in both businesses
takeaways.text: Diagnostics revenue rose 6.5% to $2,949M (4.4% organic) and Biopharma Laboratory Services rose 8.5% to $867M, as specialty testing and new health-system and pharma partnerships kept volumes climbing.

takeaways.title: Adjusted EPS rose 14.5%
takeaways.text: Adjusted EPS of $4.78 excludes $79M of intangible amortization and $16M of restructuring charges that sit in the GAAP figure of $3.22. Adjusted operating margin widened to 15.0% from 14.4%.

takeaways.title: Guidance raised
takeaways.text: Labcorp lifted its full-year outlook: revenue growth of 5.9%–6.7% and adjusted EPS of $18.30–$18.70. It also announced or closed four acquisitions in the quarter, each expected to add to adjusted EPS in year one.

oneTimers: Restructuring and other charges were $16M in the quarter (vs $6M a year ago), and GAAP results carry $79M of amortization of intangibles from past deals — both are excluded from Labcorp's adjusted EPS of $4.78.
footerNote: Labcorp reports segment revenue before intercompany eliminations: Diagnostics $2,948.9M and Biopharma Laboratory Services $866.7M, less $5.6M of eliminations and other, equals consolidated revenue of $3,810.0M (per the Q3 2026 Form 10-Q segment note). The eliminations are netted against Biopharma Laboratory Services here so the chart's segments sum to revenue. Net earnings are the consolidated $263M; $262.8M was attributable to Labcorp shareholders.
